subject: general
question: A, B, C, D, E, F and G are sitting around a circular table facing the centre. C sits third to the left of B. A sits second to the left of G. G is not an immediate neighbour of C. D sits to the immediate left of E. How many people sit between A and E when counted from the left of A?
solution:
Given: A, B, C, D, E, F and G are sitting around a circular table facing the centre.

1) C sits third to the left of B.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/17b4d128e4d622a0efb6e0e8ab593bfd6a7df03c0e49e3cba08245942942e01b.png] 

2) A sits second to the left of G. 

3) G is not an immediate neighbour of C.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/a637cb7a11610430ecfd2cd8a7bb88ece2b994be518eba7632752a41d530eb9c.png] 

4) D sits to the immediate left of E. 

After positioning E and D only one position is left which will be occupied by the only person left i.e. F.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/9e63c4b6f7ec62662d0c7238e60a99f5e941e0aca3c1181ac9c9fd28e4f28fb6.png] 

Thus, two people sit between A and E when counted from the left of A.

Hence, "Option 1" is the correct answer.
